_meta.method: complete direct literal rendering; source order preserved; no explanatory paraphrase

word_for_word: आविर्भावतिरोभावावाविष्कर्तुं स्वयं हरिः तत्त्वंपदविवेकार्थं कर्मयोगं प्रशंसति
to reveal His own manifestation and disappearance, Hari praises karma-yoga for discrimination of the meanings of ‘tat’ and ‘tvam’
एवं तावदध्यायद्वयेन कर्मयोगोपायो ज्ञानयोगोपायश्च मोक्षसाधनत्वेनोक्तः
thus in the preceding two chapters the means of karma-yoga and jñāna-yoga were taught as means to liberation
तमेव ब्रह्मार्पणादिगुणविधानेन त्वंपदार्थविवेकादिना च प्रपञ्चयिष्यन् प्रथमं तावत्परम्पराप्राप्तत्वेन स्तुवन् श्रीभगवानुवाच इममिति त्रिभिः

intending to elaborate that teaching through practices such as offering to Brahman and discrimination of the meaning of ‘tvam,’ the Blessed Lord first praises it as received through succession in three verses beginning ‘this’
अव्ययफलत्वादव्ययं इमं योगं पुराहं विवस्वते आदित्याय कथितवान्
because its fruit is imperishable, this yoga is imperishable; formerly I taught it to Vivasvān, the sun
स च स्वपुत्राय मनवे श्राद्धदेवाय प्राह स च मनुः स्वपुत्रायेक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत्
he taught it to his son Manu, Śrāddhadeva, and Manu told it to his son Ikṣvāku
एवमिति
with ‘thus’
राजानश्च त ऋषयश्चान्येऽपि राजर्षयो निमिप्रमुखाः स्वपुत्रादिभिरिक्ष्वाकुप्रमुखैः प्रोक्तमिमं योगं विदुर्जानन्ति स्म
royal sages such as Nimi, both kings and seers, knew this yoga taught by Ikṣvāku and the others to their sons and successors
अद्यतनानामज्ञाने कारणमाह हे परंतप शत्रुतापन स योगः कालवशादिह लोके नष्टो विच्छिन्नः
he states the reason for the ignorance of people today: O scorcher of foes, through the force of time this yoga became lost, its succession broken, in this world
स एवायमिति
with ‘that very one is this’
स एवायं योगोऽद्य विच्छिन्ने संप्रदाये सति पुनश्च मया ते तुभ्यमुक्तः
that very yoga, now that the tradition has been broken, has again been taught by Me to you
यतस्त्वं मम भक्तोऽसि सखा चेति अन्यस्मै मया नोच्यते
because you are My devotee and friend; I do not teach it to another
हि यस्मादिदमुत्तमं रहस्यम्
for this is the highest secret
भगवतो विवस्वन्तं प्रति योगोपदेशासंभवं पश्यन्नर्जुन उवाच अपरमिति
seeing the apparent impossibility of the Lord having taught yoga to Vivasvān, Arjuna said with ‘later’
अपरमर्वाचीनं तव जन्म परं प्राक्कालीनं विवस्वतो जन्म
Your birth is later, recent, while Vivasvān’s birth is earlier
तस्मात्तवाधुनिकत्वाच्चिरंतनाय विवस्वते त्वमादौ योगं प्रोक्तवानित्येतत्कथमहं विजानीयां ज्ञातुं शक्नुयाम्
therefore, since You are recent, how can I understand that You taught this yoga in the beginning to the ancient Vivasvān?
इति पृष्टवन्तमर्जुनं रूपान्तरेणोपदिष्टवानित्यभिप्रायेणोत्तरं श्रीभगवानुवाच बहूनीति
to Arjuna who asked thus, the Blessed Lord answers with ‘many,’ intending that He taught it in another form
मम बहूनि जन्मानि तव च व्यतीतानि
many births of Mine and yours have passed
तानि सर्वाण्यहं वेद जानामि अलुप्तविद्याशक्तित्वात्
I know them all because My power of knowledge is never lost
त्वं तु न जानासि अविद्यावृतत्वात्
but you do not know because you are covered by ignorance
नन्वनादेस्तव कुतो जन्म अविनाशिनश्च कथं पुनर्जन्म येन बहूनि मे व्यतीतानीत्युच्यते
objection: how can You who are beginningless have birth, and how can the indestructible be born repeatedly so that You say ‘many births of Mine have passed’?
ईश्वरस्य तव पुण्यपापविहीनस्य कथं जीववज्जन्मेत्यत आह अजोऽपीति
how can You, the Lord free of merit and demerit, be born like an individual soul? to this he says ‘although unborn’
सत्यमेवं तथाप्यजोऽपि सन्नहं तथाव्ययात्माप्यनश्वरस्वभावोऽपि सन् तथा ईश्वरोऽपि कर्मपारतन्त्र्यरहितोऽपि सन् स्वमायया संभवामि
this is true; nevertheless though unborn, imperishable in nature, and Lord free from dependence on karma, I manifest through My own māyā
सम्यगप्रच्युतज्ञानबलवीर्यादिशक्त्यैव भवामि
I become manifest through My own unfailing powers of knowledge, strength, valor, and the like
ननु तथापि षोडशकलात्मकलिङ्गदेहशून्यस्य तव कुतो जन्मेत्यत उक्तम्
objection: still, since You lack the subtle body composed of sixteen parts, how is birth possible? this is answered
स्वां शुद्धसत्त्वात्मिकां प्रकृतिमधिष्ठाय स्वीकृत्य विशुद्धोर्जितसत्त्वमूर्त्या स्वेच्छयावतरामीत्यर्थः
taking up My own prakṛti composed of pure sattva, I descend by My own will in a form of pure and powerful sattva; this is the meaning
कदा संभवसीत्यपेक्षायामाह यदा यदेति
when do You manifest? in answer he says ‘whenever’
धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्हानिः
decline of dharma means its diminution
अधर्मस्याभ्युत्थानमाधिक्यम्
rise of adharma means its increase
किमर्थमित्यपेक्षायामाह परित्राणायेति
for what purpose? he says ‘for protection’
साधूनां स्वधर्मवर्तिनां रक्षणाय
for protection of the good who remain in their own dharma
दुष्टं कर्म कुर्वन्तीति दुष्कृतस्तेषां वधाय च
and for destruction of evildoers, those who perform wicked actions
एवं धर्मस्य संस्थापनार्थाय साधुरक्षणेन दुष्टवधेन च धर्मं स्थिरीकर्तुं युगेयुगे तत्तदवसरे संभवामीत्यर्थः
thus I manifest age after age at the appropriate occasions to establish dharma firmly through protection of the good and destruction of the wicked; this is the meaning
नचैवं दुष्टनिग्रहं कुर्वतोऽपि नैर्घृण्यं शङ्कनीयम्
nor should cruelty be suspected even though He restrains the wicked
यथाचाहुः लालने ताडने मातुर्नाकारुण्यं यथार्भके तद्वदेव महेशस्य नियन्तुर्गुणदोषयोः
as it is said: ‘a mother is not without compassion whether caressing or striking her child; so too the Great Lord who regulates virtue and fault’
एवंविधानामीश्वरजन्मकर्मणां ज्ञाने फलमाह जन्मकर्मेति
he states the fruit of knowing divine births and actions of this kind with ‘birth and action’
मे जन्म स्वेच्छाकृतं कर्म च धर्मपालनरूपं दिव्यमलौकिकं तत्त्वतः परानुग्रहार्थमेवेति यो वेत्ति
one who knows in truth that My birth occurs by My own will and My divine, extraordinary action consists in protecting dharma solely for the grace of others
स देहाभिमानं त्यक्त्वा पुनर्जन्म नैति न प्राप्नोति किंतु मामेव प्राप्नोति
abandoning identification with the body, does not attain another birth but attains Me alone
कथं जन्मकर्मज्ञानेन त्वत्प्राप्तिः स्यादित्यत्राह वीतरागेति
how does knowing Your birth and action produce attainment of You? he says this with ‘free from attachment’
अहं शुद्धसत्त्वावतारैर्धर्मपरिपालनं करोमीति मदीयं परमकारुणिकत्वं ज्ञात्वा
knowing My supreme compassion in that I protect dharma through descents composed of pure sattva
वीता विगता रागभयक्रोधा येभ्यस्ते विक्षेपाभावात्
those from whom attachment, fear, and anger have departed, because distraction is absent
मन्मया मदेकचित्ता भूत्वा मामेवोपाश्रिताः सन्तः
becoming filled with Me, with minds fixed solely on Me, taking refuge in Me alone
मत्प्रसादलभ्यं यदात्मज्ञानं च तपश्च तत्परिपाकहेतुः स्वधर्मस्तयोर्द्वन्द्वैकवद्भावः
self-knowledge obtainable by My grace and tapas, one’s own dharma which causes its maturation, are treated together as a compound pair
तेन ज्ञानतपसा पूताः शुद्धा निरस्ताज्ञानतत्कार्यमलाः सन्तो मद्भावं मत्सायुज्यं प्राप्ता बहवः
purified by that knowledge and tapas, cleansed of ignorance and its effects, many have attained My state, union with Me
नत्वधुनैव प्रवृत्तोऽयं मद्भक्तिमार्ग इत्यर्थः
this path of devotion to Me has not begun only now; this is the meaning
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि इत्यादिना विद्याविद्योपाधिभ्यां तत्त्वंपदार्थावीश्वरजीवौ प्रदर्श्य
by ‘I know them all’ and the like, the Lord and the individual soul, meanings of ‘tat’ and ‘tvam,’ are shown through the limiting conditions of knowledge and ignorance
ईश्वरस्य चाविद्याभावेन नित्यशुद्धत्वाज्जीवस्य चेश्वरप्रसादलब्धज्ञानेनाज्ञाननिवृत्तेः शुद्धस्य सतश्चिदंशेन तदैक्यमुक्तमिति द्रष्टव्यम्

the Lord is eternally pure through absence of ignorance, and the soul becomes pure when ignorance is removed by knowledge received through the Lord’s grace; their unity in the aspect of consciousness is stated—so it should be understood
ननु तर्हि किं त्वय्यपि वैषम्यमस्ति यस्मादेवं त्वदेकशरणानामेवात्मभावं ददासि नान्येषां सकामानामित्यत आह ये यथेति
objection: then is there partiality even in You, since You grant Your state only to those solely surrendered to You and not to others who act with desire? to this he says ‘as they approach Me’
यथा येन प्रकारेण सकामतया निष्कामतया वा ये मां भजन्ति तानहं तथैव तदपेक्षितफलदानेन भजाम्यनुगृह्णामि
in whatever manner, with desire or without desire, people worship Me, I reciprocate and favor them by granting the fruit they seek
नतु ये सकामा मां विहायेन्द्रादीनेव भजन्ते तानहमुपेक्ष इति मन्तव्यम्
it should not be thought that I neglect those who, with desire, leave Me and worship Indra and the others
यतः सर्वशः सर्वप्रकारैरिन्द्रादिसेवका अपि ममैव वर्त्म भजनमार्गमनुवर्तन्ते
for in every way and manner even worshippers of Indra and the others follow My own path of worship
इन्द्रादिरूपेणापि ममैव सेव्यत्वात्
because even in the forms of Indra and the others it is I alone who am worshipped
तर्हि मोक्षार्थमेव किमिति सर्वे त्वां न भजन्तीत्यत आह काङ्क्षन्त इति
then why do all not worship You solely for liberation? to this he says ‘desiring’
कर्मणां सिद्धिं फलं काङ्क्षन्तः प्रायशः इह मनुष्यलोके इन्द्रादिदेवता एव यजन्ते नतु साक्षान्मामेव
desiring success, the fruit of actions, people in this human world mostly worship deities such as Indra and not Me directly
हि यस्मात्कर्मजा सिद्धिः कर्मजं फलं शीघ्रं भवति नतु ज्ञानफलं कैवल्यम्
because success born of action, the fruit of action, arises quickly, but not kaivalya, the fruit of knowledge
दुष्प्राप्यत्वाज्ज्ञानस्य
because knowledge is difficult to attain
ननु केचित्सकामतया प्रवर्तन्ते केचिन्निष्कामतयेति कर्मवैचित्र्यम् तत्कर्तॄणां च ब्राह्मणादीनामुत्तममध्यमादिवैचित्र्यं कुर्वतस्तव कथं वैषम्यं नास्तीत्याशङ्क्याह चातुर्वर्ण्यमिति

objection: some act with desire and others without desire, actions vary, and their performers—brāhmaṇas and others—vary as superior, intermediate, and so forth; since You create these differences, how are You impartial? anticipating this he says ‘the fourfold varṇa’
चत्वारो वर्णा एव चातुर्वर्ण्यम् स्वार्थे ष्यञ्प्रत्ययः
cāturvarṇya means simply the four varṇas; the suffix is used in its own sense
सत्त्वप्रधाना ब्राह्मणास्तेषां शमदमादीनि कर्माणि
brāhmaṇas are predominantly sattvic and their actions are tranquility, restraint, and the like
सत्त्वरजःप्रधानाः क्षत्रियास्तेषां च शौर्ययुद्धादीनि कर्माणि
kṣatriyas are predominantly sattva and rajas and their actions are valor, battle, and the like
रजस्तमःप्रधाना वैश्यास्तेषां कृषिवाणिज्यादीनि कर्माणि
vaiśyas are predominantly rajas and tamas and their actions are agriculture, trade, and the like
तमःप्रधानाः शूद्रास्तेषां च त्रैवर्णिकशुश्रूषादिकर्माणि
śūdras are predominantly tamas and their actions are service of the three varṇas and the like
इत्येवं गुणानां कर्मणां च विभागैश्चातुर्वर्ण्यं मयैव सृष्टमिति
thus the fourfold varṇa was created by Me according to divisions of guṇas and actions
सत्यम् तथाप्येवं तस्य कर्तारमपि फलतोऽकर्तारमेव मां विद्धि
true; nevertheless, though I am its creator in this way, know Me from the standpoint of result as a non-doer
तत्र हेतुः अव्ययम् आसक्तिराहित्येन श्रमरहितं नाशादिरहितम्
the reason is ‘imperishable’: free from exertion because devoid of attachment, and free from destruction and the like
तदेव दर्शयन्नाह न मामिति
showing that very point, he says ‘actions do not’
कर्माणि विश्वसृष्ट्यादीन्यपि मां न लिम्पन्ति आसक्तं न कुर्वन्ति निरहंकारत्वात्
even actions such as creation of the universe do not stain Me, do not make Me attached, because I am without ego
आप्तकामत्वेन मम कर्मफले स्पृहाभावाच्च मां न लिम्पन्तीति किं वक्तव्यम्
and since, all desires fulfilled, I have no longing for fruits of action, what need is there to say that actions do not stain Me?
यतः कर्मफले स्पृहाराहित्येन मां योऽभिजानाति सोऽपि कर्मभिर्न बध्यते
one who knows Me as free from longing for fruits of action is likewise not bound by actions
मम निर्लेपत्वे कारणं निरहंकारत्वनिःस्पृहत्वादिकं जानतस्तस्याप्यहंकारादिशैथिल्यात्
because in one who knows the causes of My unstained nature—absence of ego, desire, and the like—ego and similar bonds are loosened
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते इत्यादिचतुर्भिः श्लोकैः प्रासङ्गिकमीश्वरस्य वैषम्यं परिहृत्य पूर्वोक्तमेव कर्मयोगं प्रपञ्चयितुमनुस्मारयति एवमिति

after removing the incidental objection of partiality in the Lord through the four verses beginning ‘as they approach Me,’ he recalls the previously taught karma-yoga in order to elaborate it, with ‘thus’
अहंकारादिराहित्येन कृतं कर्म बन्धकं न भवतीत्येवं ज्ञात्वा
knowing thus that action performed without ego and the like does not bind
पूर्वैर्जनकादिभिरपि मुमुक्षुभिः सत्त्वशुद्ध्यर्थं पूर्वतरं युगान्तरेष्वपि कृतम्
it was performed long ago, even in other ages, by ancient seekers of liberation such as Janaka for purification of sattva
तस्मात्त्वमपि प्रथमं कर्मैव कुरु
therefore you too should first perform action
तच्च तत्त्वविद्भिः सह विचार्य कर्तव्यं न लोकपरम्परामात्रेणेत्याह किं कर्मेति
that action must be performed after inquiry together with knowers of truth, not merely by worldly custom; he says this with ‘what is action?’
किं कर्म कीदृशं कर्मकरणम् किमकर्म कीदृशं कर्माकरणमित्येतस्मिन्नर्थे विवेकिनोऽपि मोहिताः
even discerning persons are confused about what action is, what kind of performance counts as action, what non-action is, and what kind of non-performance counts as non-action
अतो यज्ज्ञात्वानुष्ठाय अशुभात्संसारान्मोक्ष्यसे मुक्तो भविष्यसि तत्कर्माकर्म च तुभ्यमहं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु
therefore I shall explain to you action and non-action which, when known and practiced, will free you from the inauspicious, from saṃsāra; listen
ननु लोकप्रसिद्धमेव कर्म देहादिव्यापारात्मकम् अकर्म च तदव्यापारात्मकम् अतः कथमुच्यते कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहं प्राप्ता इति तत्राह कर्मण इति
objection: action is commonly known as activity of body and the like, and non-action as absence of such activity; why then say that even the wise are confused? to this he says ‘of action’
कर्मणो विहितव्यापारस्यापि तत्त्वं बोद्धव्यमस्ति नतु लोकसिद्धमात्रमेव
the truth even of action, prescribed activity, must be understood; it is not merely what is commonly accepted
अकर्मणाऽविहितव्यापारस्यापि तत्त्वं बोद्धव्यमस्ति
the truth of non-action, activity not enjoined, must also be understood
विकर्मणोऽपि निषिद्धस्यापि तत्त्वं बोद्धव्यमस्ति
the truth of vikarma, prohibited action, must also be understood
यतः कर्मणो गतिर्गहना कर्मण इत्युपलक्षणार्थम्
because the course of action is profound; ‘action’ here is representative
कर्माकर्मविकर्मणां तत्त्वं बोद्धव्यमस्ति यतो दुर्विज्ञेयमित्यर्थः
the truth of action, non-action, and prohibited action must be understood because it is difficult to know; this is the meaning
तदेवं कर्मादीनां दुर्विज्ञेयत्वं दर्शयन्नाह कर्मण्यकर्मेति
showing thus the difficulty of knowing action and the rest, he says ‘non-action in action’
परमेश्वराराधनलक्षणे कर्मणि विषये अकर्म कर्मेदं न भवतीति यः पश्येत् तस्य ज्ञानहेतुत्वेन बन्धकत्वाभावात्
one who sees non-action in action characterized as worship of the Supreme Lord sees ‘this is not binding action,’ because as a cause of knowledge it does not bind
अकर्मणि च विहिताकरणे कर्म यः पश्येत् तस्य प्रत्यवायोत्पादकत्वेन बन्धहेतुत्वात्
and one who sees action in non-action, failure to perform what is prescribed, sees it as action because by producing adverse consequence it causes bondage
मनुष्येषु कर्मकुर्वाणेषु स बुद्धिमान् व्यवसायात्मकबुद्धिमत्त्वाच्छ्रेष्ठः
among people performing action he is intelligent, superior because he possesses resolute understanding
स युक्तः योगी तेन कर्मणा ज्ञानयोगावाप्तेः
he is disciplined, a yogin, because through that action he attains jñāna-yoga
स एव कृत्स्नकर्मकर्ता च सर्वतः संप्लुतोदकस्थानीये तस्मिन्कर्मणि सर्वकर्मफलानामन्तर्भूतत्वात्
he alone is the performer of all action because all fruits of action are included in that action, like all uses of small waters in a great flood
तदेवमारुरुक्षोः कर्मयोगाधिकारावस्थायां न कर्मणामनारम्भात् इत्यादिनोक्त एव कर्मयोगः स्फुटीकृतः
thus karma-yoga already taught for one wishing to ascend, beginning ‘not by non-performance of actions,’ is clarified
तत्प्रपञ्चरूपत्वाच्चास्य प्रकरणस्य न पौनरुक्त्यदोषः
because this section elaborates that teaching, there is no fault of repetition
अनेनैव योगारूढावस्थायां यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यात् इत्यादिना यः कर्मानुपयोग उक्तस्तस्याप्यर्थात्प्रपञ्चः कृतो वेदितव्यः
by this, the non-necessity of action for one established in yoga, stated with ‘but he whose delight is in the Self,’ should also be understood as elaborated by implication
यदा आरुरुक्षोरपि कर्म बन्धकं न भवति तदा आरूढस्य कुतो बन्धकं स्यात्
if action does not bind even one wishing to ascend, how could it bind one already established?
यद्वा कर्मणि देहेन्द्रियादिव्यापारे वर्तमानोऽप्यात्मनो देहादिव्यतिरेकानुभवेनाकर्म स्वाभाविकं नैष्कर्म्यमेव यः पश्येत्
or, while engaged in bodily and sensory activity, one sees natural non-action, naiṣkarmya, through direct experience that the Self is distinct from body and the rest
तथा कर्मणि च ज्ञानरहिते दुःखबुद्ध्या कर्मणां त्यागे कर्म यः पश्येत् तस्य प्रतिबन्धकत्वेन मिथ्याचारत्वात्
and one sees action in the abandonment of action made from aversion and without knowledge, because such abandonment is obstructive and hypocritical
तदुक्तं कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् इति
as stated: ‘he who restrains the organs of action but sits remembering with the mind’
य एवंभूतः स तु सर्वेषु मनुष्येषु बुद्धिमान् पण्डितः
one of this kind is intelligent, learned, among all people
तत्र हेतुः कृत्स्नानि सर्वाणि यदृच्छया प्राप्तान्याहारादीनि कर्माणि कुर्वन्नपि स युक्त एवाकर्त्रात्मज्ञानेन समाधिस्थ एवेत्यर्थः
the reason: though performing all actions such as eating that arise of themselves, he remains disciplined and established in samādhi through knowledge of the Self as non-doer; this is the meaning
अनेनैव ज्ञानिनः स्वभावादापन्नं कलञ्जभक्षणादिकं न दोषाय अज्ञस्य तु रागतः कृतं दोषायेति विकर्मणोऽपि तत्त्वं निरूपितं द्रष्टव्यम्

by this it should also be understood that prohibited action such as eating forbidden food occurring naturally for a knower is not a fault, while for the ignorant person done from attachment it is a fault; thus the truth of vikarma too is explained
